text:
mira: thinking about an nsys capture workflow to isolate kernel selection vs kv-cache eviction. big qdreps are noisy and slow to inspect, wondering if we should do multi-window captures

devon: +1 to multi-window. smaller windows are easier to diff. i usually do warmup window, steady-state capture, then a short tail capture for evictions

josh: agree. trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt is the usual combo. nvtx bracketing lets you cut out everything else in the UI

mira: curious about overlap strategy — do people do back-to-back windows or overlapping windows to catch handoffs?

anika: overlapping by ~200-500ms helped me once when handoff jittered across calls. keeps both sides visible without huge files

mira: here's a capture pattern i sketched (pseudo command):

```
nsys profile --output=out_probe1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \  --capture-range=nvtx \  --capture-range-start=nvtx:WARMUP_START \  --capture-range-end=nvtx:WARMUP_END \  --duration=10s \  --compress=true -- <server binary args>
```

devon: a few practical tips:
- keep each window ~8-15s (too short -> sampling noise, too long -> huge qdrep)
- use NVTX push/pop around the exact code paths (e.g., batch fill, kv lookup, eviction)
- record at least one capture with only trace=cuda,nvtx (no osrt) to see kernel shapes without OSRT markers

josh: also capture an isolated warmup run with ./perf-wrapper --no-batching so kernels are easier to map to ops (helps kernel selection debugging)

mira: file-size / UI perf question: compress flag helps but qdrep can still be ~100s MB. any heuristics to reduce size?

anika: filter by pid when possible, and avoid system-wide capture. nvtx-bracketed captures + --trace=cuda,nvtx (skip osrt if not needed) reduces noise a lot

perf-bot: FYI: when you use overlapping windows, make sure your NVTX IDs are monotonic or annotated, otherwise UI zoom+compare gets confusing

devon: last gotcha — if you suspect kernel selection regressions, export kernel timeline CSV from the UI and diff by name+start_time to catch micro-swaps (e.g., float->int kernel variant change)

mira: great, i'll run a series: warmup-only, steady-state 12s, overlapping handoff 3x windows. will post qdrep snippets and kernel timeline CSVs

josh: good plan. ping me when you have the csvs, i can run a quick grep for kernel names like MHA, fused_matmul, kv_lookup to see if selection changed

anika: and add a capture with nvprof/perfetto if you want system counters and thread scheduling info — sometimes the perf reg drops are due to CPU scheduling not GPU kernels

mira: thanks all, i'll upload results to the thread (small snippets and the csv diffs).
